```{r}

#Load necessary packages
if(!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(deSolve,
               tidyverse,
               here
               )
 
```

```{r}
# Load the CSV file and assign it to a variable named 'seir_data'
seir_data <- read.csv("SIR.csv")

```



```{r}
# Setting up the SEIR Model in R----

  # STEP 1: Set up initial conditions and parameters
# Create vector/variable called initial state 
initial_state <- c(S = 999, E = 0, I = 1, R = 0)
initial_state

# Define the values of transmission (beta), incubation (sigma), and recovery (gamma) parameters
# Create vector/variable parameters
parameters <- c(beta  = 0.0025,
                sigma = 0.5,   # Average incubation of 2 days = 1/2 = 0.5
                gamma = 0.2)   # Sick for 5 days = 1/5 = 0.2
parameters

# Set the time span starting at 0 
time <- seq(0, 365, by = 1) 
time

```


```{r}
#STEP 2: Write the SEIR Model function
#Define function and arguments
seir_model <- function(time, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {

    # Rate of change
    dS <- -beta * S * I          # Susceptible individuals become Exposed
    dE <-  beta * S * I - sigma * E  # Exposed individuals move to Infected at rate sigma
    dI <-  sigma * E - gamma * I # Infected individuals recover at rate gamma
    dR <-  gamma * I             # Recovered individuals accumulate

    # Return the rates of change in the exact order of states vector
    list(c(dS, dE, dI, dR))
  })
}
 
```


```{R}
  #STEP 3: Solve the differential equations using deSolve and ODE function
#create object with solutions for differential equations
seir_out <- ode(
  y = initial_state,
  time = time,
  func = seir_model,
  parms = parameters
)

seir_out
```


```{R}
  #STEP 4: Convert the output to a data frame
seir_out <- as.data.frame(seir_out)
seir_out
```

```{R}
# VISUALIZE THE RESULTS
# Create a plot to visualize the dynamics of the SEIR model
ggplot(seir_out, aes(x = time)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = S, color = "Susceptible"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = E, color = "Exposed"), linewidth = 1) +     
  geom_line(aes(y = I, color = "Infected"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = R, color = "Recovered"), linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "SEIR Model Simulation",                          
       x = "Time (days)",
       y = "Population Count",
       color = "Compartments") +                                 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Susceptible" = "#2F5597", 
                                "Exposed"     = "#ED7D31",       
                                "Infected"    = "#C00000",
                                "Recovered"   = "#548235")) +
  theme_minimal()

```  


```{R}
#Load observed data
observed_data <- read.csv(here("SIR.csv"))
observed_data 
```  


```{R}
# Create a comparison graph
comparison_graph <- 
  ggplot() +
  # 1. Observed data: Plotting time (X) vs total active observed infections (Ia + Is)
  geom_line(data = observed_data,
            aes(x = X, y = Ia + Is, color = "Observed Data (Ia + Is)"),
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = observed_data,
             aes(x = X, y = Ia + Is, color = "Observed Data (Ia + Is)"),
             size = 2) +
  
  # 2. SEIR Model Output: Plotting simulation time vs the Infectious tracking (I)
  geom_line(data = seir_out,            
            aes(x = time, y = I, color = "SEIR Model Forecast (I)"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Styling colors and layout aesthetics
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Observed Data (Ia + Is)" = "black", 
                                "SEIR Model Forecast (I)" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "SEIR Model Fit vs. Observed Active Cases",
    x = "Time (Days)",
    y = "Active Infectious Count",
    color = "Data Stream"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


#load the graph  
comparison_graph

```
